subject.title: Feature: diagnostics stuck-session recovery ladder (steer → nudge → abort)

question: Should OpenClaw own an automatic in-process staged recovery policy for stalled sessions, and if so, which mutations are safe before abort-drain and under what Gateway-liveness conditions?
rationale: The requested behavior adds new autonomous mutations and configuration to a core session-recovery path. Source and related incident evidence establish the available primitives and safety hazard, but cannot decide the acceptable user-visible recovery policy.

options.title: Stage diagnosis before mutation
options.body: Sponsor the read-only diagnosis work first, then define a narrow recovery-policy proposal using its stable findings and liveness predicates before adding steer or nudge automation.

options.title: Adopt an internal recovery ladder
options.body: Define an owner-controlled core state machine with liveness gating, idempotent action records, and explicit delivery rules, then implement it as a focused follow-up.

options.title: Keep recovery operator-driven
options.body: Retain abort-drain plus explicit operator session controls and document an external operational workflow rather than introducing automated pre-abort mutations.

recommendation.title: Stage diagnosis before mutation
recommendation.body: Sponsor the read-only diagnosis work first, then define a narrow recovery-policy proposal using its stable findings and liveness predicates before adding steer or nudge automation.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a core product and operator-safety choice rather than a localized bug repair.
